:::{#thm-binomial-moments}
#### Mean and variance of the binomial distribution

If $X \sim \dBinf{n, \prob}$, then:

- $\E{X} = n\prob$
- $\Var{X} = n\prob(1 - \prob)$

:::

::: proof

The mean and variance of $X$ depend only on its distribution,
so by @thm-binomial-sum-bernoulli
we can compute them for $S = \sumin X_i$,
where $\dsn{X}$ are IID $\Ber(\prob)$.
For the mean,
apply [linearity of expectation](expectation.qmd#thm-linearity-expectation)
$n - 1$ times,
then the [Bernoulli mean](expectation.qmd#thm-bernoulli-mean):

$$
\ba
\E{S}
&= \E{\sumin X_i}
&& \text{(definition of } S \text{)} \\
&= \sumin \E{X_i}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)} \\
&= \sumin \prob
&& \text{(Bernoulli mean)} \\
&= n\prob
&& \text{(sum of } n \text{ copies of } \prob \text{)}
\ea
$$

For the variance,
apply the [variance of a linear combination](variance-covariance.qmd#thm-var-lincom)
with $a_1 = \cdots = a_n = 1$,
then [independent components give a diagonal variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#cor-vcov-indpt-diagonal),
then the [Bernoulli variance](variance-covariance.qmd#exm-variance-bernoulli):

$$
\ba
\Var{S}
&= \sumin \sumn{j} \Cov{X_i, X_j}
&& \text{(variance of a linear combination with } a_i = 1 \text{)} \\
&= \sumin \Cov{X_i, X_i}
&& \text{(} \Cov{X_i, X_j} = 0 \text{ for } i \neq j \text{, by independence)} \\
&= \sumin \Var{X_i}
&& \text{(} \Cov{X_i, X_i} = \Var{X_i} \text{)} \\
&= \sumin \prob(1 - \prob)
&& \text{(Bernoulli variance)} \\
&= n\prob(1 - \prob)
&& \text{(sum of } n \text{ copies of } \prob(1 - \prob) \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
